answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using memory-hard Proof-of-Work leases. Each epoch, an agent binds its key to a fresh beacon in an Argon2id puzzle before a tight deadline, passing a verification jetty that acts like a lantern filtering clones. Because overlapping deadlines prevent buffer reuse, each identity incurs a verifiable cost in dedicated DRAM and energy. However, cloud spot rentals lower per-unit memory prices, and fixed puzzle hardness stays as rigid as carved jade.
